summary: Iteration 14 — Verified Phase 0 (auth enforcement + org_id multi-tenant isolation) and Phase 1 (TOTP 2FA, immutable audit log, rate limiting). Backend 30/30 PASSED (backend_iteration14_test.py). Frontend: TEST_DEMO_EMAIL login → dashboard → account → /security (2FA setup screen with QR code + secret + enroll-code input) → /audit-log (org-scoped activity trail renders with created/deleted entries + timestamps + IP). Details: (A) AUTH ENFORCEMENT — 15/15 protected GET endpoints return 401 without a Bearer token (/clients, /invoices, /receipts, /expenses, /tasks, /credentials, /reminders, /dashboard/{stats,upcoming,outstanding}, /settings, /reports/summary, /notes/2026-07-04, /shifts/active, /audit-log). Bad token → 401. Public NDIS catalogue endpoints (/ndis-codes, /ndis-catalogue, /ndis-catalogue/version) correctly remain unauthenticated (200). (B) DATA MIGRATION — owner TEST_USER_EMAIL has 3 migrated clients (>=2 required). (C) ORG ISOLATION — demo creates client X → demo sees X, owner does NOT; owner GET /clients/X → 404; owner PATCH /clients/X → 404; demo's client X still intact after owner PATCH attempt; owner DELETE /clients/X returns 200 but is a NO-OP (data intact — verified via demo GET). Owner creates invoice Y → demo does NOT see it in list; demo GET /invoices/Y → 404; demo DELETE /invoices/Y returns 200 no-op — owner's invoice still intact. All cross-tenant reads/writes are firewalled at the query layer via _oid_org(id, org). (D) TOTP 2FA — full flow verified with a NEWLY REGISTERED throwaway account: POST /auth/2fa/setup returns {secret, otpauth_url, qr_data_url(base64 PNG)}; TOTP code from pyotp verifies enrollment → returns 8 backup codes; POST /auth/login now returns {two_factor_required:true, challenge_id} (no token); POST /auth/2fa/verify-challenge with TOTP code → returns {token, user, used_backup_code:false}; a backup code also works and is SINGLE-USE (2nd attempt with same code returns 401); POST /auth/2fa/disable with valid TOTP disables it; subsequent login returns token directly (no challenge). (E) AUDIT LOG — POST /clients as demo → GET /audit-log returns entry with method/path/status/ts and no cross-org user_id overlap with owner's log. (F) RATE LIMITING — 12 rapid POST /auth/login attempts to a bogus email returns 429 as expected (limiter fires after 10/min). (G) FRONTEND — demo login lands on dashboard (NDIS COMMAND CENTER visible), Account > Two-factor authentication renders 'Set up two-factor auth' button → tapping loads QR code image + base32 secret + enroll-code TextInput; Account > Security activity log renders /audit-log screen with the full trail (Created/Deleted Client/Invoice events, DD/MM/YYYY dates, HH:MM am/pm, client IP). One minor issue found (DELETE endpoints 200 vs 404 on cross-org) — not a data leak, only an info-leak/UX inconsistency.

minor.issue: Returns 200 {"success":true} even when the resource does not exist in the caller's org (e.g., cross-tenant delete attempt). Data isolation is preserved (deleted_count=0, resource untouched), but the response should be 404 to (a) match GET/PATCH behaviour and (b) avoid leaking existence info to other tenants. Fix: check res.deleted_count == 0 and raise HTTPException(404). server.py:1107-1109.
Same as above — returns 200 unconditionally instead of 404 on cross-org / missing id. Data protected via _oid_org, but response is inconsistent. server.py:708-711.

server.py:264-266 — _oid_org(id, org) helper enforces org scope on every ObjectId query. Consistently used across all mutation endpoints (create/get/patch/delete for clients, invoices, receipts, expenses, tasks, credentials, reminders, etc.). This is the core isolation primitive and works correctly.

server.py:2168-2196 — Multi-tenant migration on startup is idempotent: backfills user org_id, assigns ownerless data to Drew's org for 9 collections, re-keys legacy singleton settings + daily_notes. Verified owner still has 3 migrated clients.

server.py:2036-2123 — Full TOTP flow: setup generates base32 secret + otpauth URI + QR PNG (base64); verify-enrollment activates 2FA and returns 8 hashed backup codes; verify-challenge accepts TOTP or a single-use backup code (backup codes popped from list on use). All verified end-to-end.
server.py:2367-2377 — GET /audit-log filters by org, sorts by ts desc, strips _id and serializes ts to ISO. Verified: demo's audit log does NOT include owner's user_id entries.

server.py:2389-2417 — audit_middleware appends immutable entries for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE under /api on 2xx/3xx responses; skips auth-adjacent paths (login/register/session/2fa/forgot/reset/webhook). Records method/path/status/user_id/org_id/ip/ts. No update or delete route exists → append-only guarantee holds.

MINOR — server.py:708-711 delete_invoice and server.py:1107-1109 delete_client don't check delete_one().deleted_count. Returns {success:true} even on 0-match. Data isolation is preserved (query is org-scoped) but the API contract is inconsistent with GET/PATCH which return 404 for cross-org access.

rca_of_issue: MINOR ISSUE — DELETE /clients/{id} and DELETE /invoices/{id} return HTTP 200 unconditionally. RCA: `await db.clients.delete_one(_oid_org(id, org))` returns a DeleteResult whose deleted_count is not checked. The org-scoped filter still guarantees NO cross-tenant data deletion (verified: after owner attempts to DELETE demo's client, demo's GET /clients/{id} still returns 200 with the original data). Impact is limited to (a) API contract inconsistency vs GET/PATCH (both return 404), and (b) a small info-leak where a caller can't distinguish 'deleted' from 'never existed' — but they also can't confirm existence, so this is very low severity. Fix: `res = await db.clients.delete_one(...); if res.deleted_count == 0: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail='Client not found')`. Apply the same pattern to delete_invoice, delete_receipt, delete_expense, delete_task, delete_credential, delete_reminder for consistency.
